utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I've heard of no preliminaries. The Chamber was informed that there's a slight change in the sequence of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Next witness to be RM003. Then could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could make use of time while we're waiting for the witness. I, at least, was not informed of a change in sequence of the witnesses, so perhaps if -- if the other side can advise us what that change is so we can make sure that the appropriate personnel are here for those witnesses as Mr. Lukic is not in the courtroom at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Lukic was sent an e-mail last evening, which I believe the Chamber was also sent, so it's a reversal of the next two witnesses. There are two witnesses remaining after this witness for the week. If I can just have a moment, I'll just refresh my memory as to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Those are the two witnesses that we will be reversing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hurko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hurko, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. That is, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Ivetic will now continue his cross-examination on behalf of the Mladic Defence. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Since we will be dealing with your signed witness statement, sir, I wanted to see if you have a copy of it in front of you. If not, I do have a clean copy in the B/C/S language that I can provide for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please provide it to the witness. Any need it to be shown to the Prosecution or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: We accept Mr. Ivetic's representation that it's a clean copy, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if we could start off at paragraph 1 of your statement. You mention that on the 2nd of April, 1992, when you took the bus home to Rogatica from Sarajevo that Serb soldiers stopped you at Stjenice. They searched and checked the identities of people.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Excuse me. If it would be possible to also put it up in -- up on the screen in e-court so that everybody else can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. That's P164.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, am I correct that these Serb soldiers searched and checked the identities of people but otherwise that you had no problems with them?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I also correct that these soldiers checked the identities -- I apologise. I'm told that there was no translation for Mr. Mladic, so I'm going to have to repeat that question, sir, and please bear with me. Am I correct that these Serb soldiers searched and checked the identities of people but otherwise that you had no problems with them?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that these soldiers checked the identification papers of all the people on the bus?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you know, were the people on the bus, did they include persons of all ethnicities or nationalities?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think it was different, but -- I don't know. Everybody showed their own documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then the soldiers just let you go; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did let us go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for a point of clarification, were these JNA soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Camouflage military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now I'd like to go back to a document that you mention in your statement, P166. That is an item that you discuss in paragraph 4 of your witness statement. And it has been introduced into evidence. In your statement, you state that you knew of no enemy strongholds in this area, that is to say May 22nd, 1992. Isn't it true, sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we also have P166 on the screens so we're able to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It's a one-page document in both the English and the B/C/S, so everything is going to be on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document is dated the 23rd of May, 1992. Would you agree with me that at that time in the area of Rogatica municipality and, in fact, in some of these settlements that are listed in this document, these villages had armed guards or watches in place --

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you wait for me to finish the question, sir. Would you agree with me that these villages had armed guards or watches in place similar to the one that you were part of?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about these guards. When I came to the village of Madjar, we'd gathered around the houses. That's where we stood guard duty. That's what we called it at any rate. I had a pistol. Somebody had a hunting gun. Nothing. Those were these village guards. And now you're talking as if these were some special guards. It was nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for the answer, sir. Now if we look at this document briefly, the middle of the page in both languages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, there may be some confusion. It's not entirely clear whether the answer to your last question relates to the other villages or to the witness's own village. Witness, could you tell us were you told that -- that you stood guard duty in your own village, do you know whether the same was done in the other villages of the municipality? Do you know or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in these nearby villages, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean you know that they stood guard in a similar way in those nearby villages. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, and thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, if I can direct you to this -- to the middle of this document in both languages, there's talk about the body of a Serb soldier that had been in possession of the enemy forces being recovered. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would also focus your attention to the end of that paragraph where it says: "In the rear, enemy forces killed two old men." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, sir, that this text would seem to suggest that someone was armed and was fighting against the Serb forces in Rogatica at the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. May I explain this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that question. I think the document speaks for itself in terms of what it suggests and the witness isn't being asked for his own knowledge on the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I may respond, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may respond, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This document was presented by the Office of the Prosecution through this witness. This document was admitted into evidence by the Office of the Prosecution with respect to this witness. Counsel asked this witness about the comment that there were about -- there being no enemy forces in the village and that these villages were attacked. Therefore, it is quite relevant to address this witness, the credibility of his testimony on that record, and again this is a matter that was opened up in direct examination by counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think Ms. Hochhauser did not object on the basis of relevance. She was objecting on the basis of that we shouldn't ask a witness to interpret a document, what it suggests, does not, because that is to be derived from the text itself. At the same time, I noticed that apparently the witness was starting an answer in which he explains what his observations were. So therefore, if you would have phrased your question in a different way. And that's, of course, what the Prosecution did. They elicited from the witness factual comment on what is described here. If he says there were no enemy strongholds, that is his own observation and is not interpreting the text. Therefore, please rephrase your question in such a way that the issue is dealt with but not by asking the witness to tell what the text suggests, because that is what the Chamber can identify itself as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, having viewed this text, would you care to -- and having refreshed your recollection with this text, would you care to revise your prior answer that there were no enemy strongholds in this area?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no enemy strongholds in that area. But may I explain this document that you've come up?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, sir, the Judges and the Prosecution do not want you to explain the document. I will ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Don't explain the document, but tell us what you knew about matters described in this document. Please do.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The village of Zlatni Do, where this soldier got killed, as they were saying -- I don't know that he got killed. But anyway, if he got killed, this is a place on the outskirts of Rogatica. All the refugees fleeing from Rogatica before the war and during the war had to go through this Zlatni Do. That is where they came across land-mines. Some got killed, some got injured, lost their legs, Muslims, women, children. Now, whether this soldier was supposed to be there, whether he was on patrol duty, I don't know. But I don't know why he would be there in the first place and what he was doing there. I don't know. Possibly somebody killed him too, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so you have no knowledge of the event, but you told us that mines were there --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- which caused several people to be injured including children --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- and women. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's avoid a battle about what seems to be semantic, what is a military stronghold and what is the presence of armed persons. That, of course, not exactly the same, and therefore to invite the witness to revise his answer on the basis of what seems to be at least some -- some victims and some shooting and to have armed military strongholds. That's, of course, to some extent a semantic issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It is, Your Honour. And I hope that within a few moments we'll have a much clearer picture as I get into matters that the Office of the Prosecutor excluded from the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're looking forward to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, is it your testimony that you have no knowledge of any existing armed Bosnian Muslim forces operating in Rogatica municipality in the Muslim villages in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry -- I'm sorry, Mr. Ivetic. That's not what the witness said. The witness said there are no enemy strongholds in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that's why I'm asking this question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But you're asking him about -- that's not your question. Your question is does -- is it your testimony that you have no knowledge of any existing armed Bosnian Muslim forces. That's something different from strong enemy holds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, I think that if you have phrased the question like: Do you have any knowledge of, and leaving out whether that's the testimony of the witness, then we also avoid any discussion or whether it is the testimony to be given by the witness or the testimony already given by the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- would avoid that problem. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any knowledge of existing armed Bosnian Muslim forces operating in Rogatica municipality in the Muslim villages in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In May 1992, I've already said there were armed Muslims without uniforms. The police that fled from Rogatica had automatic weapons. I also saw hunting weapons, I saw some M48 rifles in the hands of civilians. And as for strongholds, I saw trenches. I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm a bit confused by the last two lines: "And as for strongholds," you say, "I saw trenches." And then you said: "I did not see that." Is that -- did you see the trenches or did you not see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not see trenches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I don't think you understood the Judge's question. Isn't it true that you dug trenches in the villages above Radici in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I went from the village of Madjar and when I came to the village of Radic. I was there around the 20th of July. That's when it was. I got this written on an ordinary piece of paper with a pencil to report to Novakovici. When I arrived there I saw about 400 milled-aged men. There was a commander there. They called him Commander Husein Hadzibulic and Ljubomir Muhamed was his deputy. They said that those who had weapons should go to one side and those who did not have weapons should go to the other side. I went to this other side because I did not have a weapon so half of the people there were armed. When I say "armed," I mean people who had hunting rifles; automatic rifles, that's what the police had who had fled. This Hadzibulic talked to them and said that Chetniks were attacking us, that we left our homes. We have no homes. We have 10 kilometres more to the Drina and we have to jump into the Drina. As for the rest, those who do not have weapons, they would be in the work platoon. I left -- I went away from there. I went to my children and nobody said anything. We were there in the woods, about ten or 12 of us, and we went to dig some trench, just like that. Just so as not to be totally idle. It was just like that. And also one day we made a road. We got together with shovels, whatever, and that's what we did. Nobody called me up and said you're in a work platoon and now you have to report every day so on and so forth. So within 20 odd-days I already fell prisoner. Later on, I heard that it was called work obligation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, this that you've just told us -- first of all, for the record, am I correct that at this time when you went to the village of Radici, you joined the so-called Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Territorial Defence force under Mr. Husein Hadzibulic?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's it. Do you understand that? That's when I was called to come there. I mean, you know, I came there for that lineup and I didn't go anywhere else except for those two days when I did that work.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough and was Mr. Hadzibulic's unit operating on the territory of the Muslim villages in Rogatica community in the period of May 1992 through August 1992 when you were captured?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, no. That's the first time I saw Husein Hadzibulic. I mean, I don't know what they were doing there. I went back into the forest where my children were. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I do, sir, and I will get to all of that, trust me. This portion, all this portion is not in your statement. Did -- did you omit this from your statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Based on?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I don't understand what he means by did he omit this from the written statement. The written statement was prepared as an amalgamation of his prior statements which contain the information and have been disclosed to counsel and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're more --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, now are you answering the question more or less and that's not what you're supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, could you rephrase your question in such a way that we know how this statement was taken, who took initiative to do what.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we are now talking about P164. That is the statement of which you have a hard copy in front of you, just so that there's no confusion. In the process of preparing that statement, did you tell the personnel from the Office of the Prosecutor this -- this information about Mr. Husein Hadzibulic, about the 400 members of this Territorial Defence of the Republic of BiH armed with the armaments that you mentioned. Did you provide that information to the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read this statement, and -- I mean ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we went through a rather significant amount of corrections that you made to this statement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, this is not about corrections. It is about selection of topics in a statement, and that's a different matter from a correction. May I inquire with the parties first. Mr. Ivetic, your knowledge of what apparently is not in the statement, is that based on any previous statement or any previous testimony of the witness which was disclosed to the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then therefore there's no way of not disclosing matters, but, rather, a matter of selecting what the Prosecution considers to be the most relevant; whereas, the Defence is aware of other periods, other places, about which the witness testified. If you consider that to be relevant, then you may elicit evidence on that rather than to start exploring on who left it out on purpose because that's clearly the suggestion you are making. Please elicit from the witness whatever evidence you consider to be relevant. And if it would not have been in one of the previous statements, then that might have been different. But apparently the Prosecution has been transparent by providing you with previous statements, which includes those portions which it now apparently considers to be less relevant as evidence in the present case. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell me what day and what month it was that you first went to Radici and were -- first joined the Territorial Defence of the Republic of BiH?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of June, the 8th of June, when the attack on Madjari commenced. We couldn't go into our house, so I went to Radici with my children. It was about the 8th of June that I left the village of Madjar. And the lining up I mentioned took place on, roughly speaking, the 20th of July. I spoke about that just a while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You have mentioned a lineup. I would like to show you a document that's been marked 65 ter number 1D111.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And this will be the first page in e-court for both the B/C/S and the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now this is dated the 29th of April, 1992, sir, and it's a telex sent from the Staff of the Territorial Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina by Mr. Hasan Efendic. It describes calls for co-ordinated action with the Ministry of Interior to blockade roads and the prevention of movements by the JNA, as well as co-ordinating and planning military action across the entire territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Sir, did the lineup where Commander Husein Hadzibulic lined you and other members -- other individuals up, did it include instruction on any of these matters contained in this order from Mr. Hasan Efendic?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know anything about this document. I wasn't there. I've already said that from the 20th of July, 1992, I was part of that unit. I joined the unit. And for 20 days, I was free. As of that day later, I was taken captive. I was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, am I correct that in Rogatica the MUP or the police forces split into two; that is, that there was a Serb element and a Muslim element that co-existed at the same time in --

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I left Rogatica on the 6th of April, and I don't know what took place in the town of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to call up -- this document I do not intend to tender, Your Honours, as the witness has said he had no knowledge of it so we can move along. I'd like to call up 65 ter number 1D176.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, while we wait for this document, I think you will see that this is also dated the 29th of April, 1992, and it's from the MUP of the Republic of BiH, and we can see from the original that Mr. Alija Delimustafic signed it. And it talks about the same situation as in the prior document but this time on the side of the so-called Bosnian Muslim MUP. I want to ask you: You mentioned police officers being present at the lineup. Am I to understand you correctly that we are talking about Bosnian Muslim MUP members that were present in the lineup of 400 persons by Commander Hadzibulic?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were some policemen from the Rogatica MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And these policemen were armed with automatic infantry weapons; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did see automatic infantry weapons. I only saw such weapons on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you about Ramiz Alajbegovic. Am I correct that this person was the former deputy chief of the police station in Rogatica and after the split became chief of the Bosnian Muslim component of the police in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the war, I think that Ramiz was the commander of the police, not the chief, or perhaps the deputy. But later he became the commander of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you agree with me that this police, commanded by Mr. Alajbegovic, was in existence and was operating armed in the Muslim villages of Rogatica municipality during the time-period of May through August 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were in those Muslim villages in the municipality of Rogatica. But they weren't all in the area where I was present. It was in the other area in the direction of Sokolac. So they weren't all in the area where I was present. Nothing was known at the time and everyone went where they could.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about something that I believe you do know about. Am I correct that your father assisted Mr. Alajbegovic to recruit villages in the Rogatica municipality to join the so-called Territorial Defence of the Republic of BiH and planned to engage in combat with the VRS?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, this is how it was. My father on several occasions went to Madjar from the village of Radici. He went there to fetch food and so on. On one occasion when he was passing by he met Ramiz Alajbegovic, and Ramiz Alajbegovic asked him whether he could meet up with the Lelek family who lived by our village. He said, I'll see. If you can do so, try and meet them. And when he was passing by, he saw one of the Lelek family members. And there was an agreement that Ramiz Alajbegovic and my father and several members of the Lelek family should meet. And then a day or two later, as agreed, they had a meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I urge both counsel and the witness to slow down when they speak. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that the Lelek village turned down the request of Ramiz Alajbegovic to join the so-called Territorial Defence of the Republic of BiH?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they met Ramiz Alajbegovic asked them whether they would be willing to join the TO to defend an integral Bosnia-Herzegovina. They said that this was a war between the Muslims and the Serbs but everyone was going over to their own side and they didn't accept that offer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I want to clear up something. And, again, this will be the last -- well, strike that. Let me see, I'll try to move on. You've answered some of the questions I'd already thought of asking you now. If I can ask you, sir: You testified in the Karadzic proceedings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you about one aspect of that testimony which took place on the 2nd of September, 2011. It's at transcript page 18223, lines 14 to line 25. And, sir, in so far as there are no transcripts in the -- in the language that you understand, I'm going to have to ask you to please listen carefully to what I read to you from that, and then I'll ask you about one particular aspect of that testimony. If I may then begin, sir, if you're ready?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you are aware that when reading usually the speed of speech goes up, so please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: All right. Sir, now I'm beginning the quotation: "A. The 22nd of May, I was in the village of Madjar where my father lived. On that day, around 1300 hours, fire was opened on all Muslim villages in the municipality of Rogatica; that is to say, literally all of them. And that is when that happened for the first time. "Q. How do you know that fire was opened on all the Muslim villages in the municipality of Rogatica? "A. The village of Madjar is up on a hill, and you can see all of Rogatica and the other villages like Kovalj, Vragolovi, Kopljevici, Orahovo, Sljedovici, Tubrici. All of these villages could be seen, and you could see the shells falling on all of these villages. You could see all of that from this village of mine where I was, Madjar, and all these shells were falling in Madjar," end quote, sir. And the question I have for you is: In this statement in this case, you very clearly state that it was small arms fire that occurred on the 22nd of May, and that is at paragraph 3 of the statement. Would you therefore have to correct the testimony that you gave in the Karadzic case regarding shells falling on Madjar?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I would just ask, if I may, that the witness's statement at paragraph 3 be on the screen, made available to him, since that's where the portion is that counsel is referring him to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think he was provided with a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe he still has a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you have a look at paragraph 3, Witness. Especially the first few lines. Could you comment on what Mr. Ivetic just read as your testimony in the other case and what you stated in paragraph 3 as to the weaponry used on the 22nd of May, 1992? Small arms fire, or shelling.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were from Serbian places, where Serbs lived. And they fired from those places on Muslim villages. All the surrounding Muslim villages that I have enumerated. And they fired from small weapons and from -- they fired shells on all these villages that I have enumerated. The Muslims didn't open fire here. And it wasn't until the 10th of August, 1992 -- or prior to that date I didn't see a single mortar or artillery in possession of the Muslims. The largest weapons that I saw were automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. The one issue raised at this moment is that the fire that was opened on your village, in your statement it reads that it was small-arms fire - that should be fire from the opposite armed forces; whereas, in your testimony in the Karadzic case, you said it was shelling. Could you explain the difference between your testimony in Karadzic and what we find in your statement at this moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were these small weapons and then there were shells that were fired, and then there were these infantry weapons, as I have said. But shells fell on the villages. I don't know how I put it previously, but shells did fall on various places, that's quite certain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your statement is, in that respect, incomplete? Where it only refers to heavy small-arms fire.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I didn't put it clearly. I am saying now that I do remember that there was shelling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you believe perhaps that you did mention it and it was a translation error, the shelling, and that's why it's not in the statement that the Office of the Prosecutor introduced into evidence?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what happened, but things were the way I have just described them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document that we've marked -- that is marked 65 ter number 08359.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is a document on the Prosecution's list. And for now, if we can have the top of the first page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: First of all, sir, looking at the top of this document, could you verify if, in fact, you are the citizen listed there, Sefik Hurko, son of Fejzo and Izeta, born 22nd November, 1957, in Rogatica, who is giving this statement?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall giving a statement in November of 1994 at the premises of the security --

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I would ask you to wait for my question to be asked in its entirety and then to please answer, otherwise we'll just have more confusion and it will take more time to get through this. Do you recall giving a statement in November 1994 at the premises of the Security Services Centre in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just so that we can be sure, at the time that you gave this statement, would it be accurate to state that the Security Service Centre in Sarajevo was subordinated under the government of Mr. Alija Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I don't know who they were subordinated to. I don't know anything about politics. I believe that that was the case, but I don't know who was subordinated to whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could turn to the middle of the first paragraph in the English and it's also the middle of the first paragraph in the B/C/S, and I will read the English, and, sir, hopefully you can locate this on the B/C/S, although it is a rather poor copy. The part I'm interested in starts: "As soon as we arrived in the village, we organised night watches together with the other inhabitants. We were poorly armed, and I had a CZ57, 7.62-millimetre pistol. It was relatively calm until 22 May 1992, when heavy small-arms fire was opened on our village from the surrounding hills." Sir, would you agree with me that there is a distinct difference between heavy small-arms fire and shelling that you have described today?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I would agree that there is a distinction to be made. But I didn't express myself very well. I didn't know much about the infantry or about the artillery and so on and so forth at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this statement was made two years - and we're talking now about the statement on the screen from 1994 - was made two years after the incident in question. Would you agree with me that your memory of events was better in 1994, when you gave this statement, as opposed to 2011 in the Karadzic case or today, when you testified about there being shelling?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I was in a worse state then. I had come out of a camp and for about 26 months I suffered a lot. If you read about this in the statements, you will know. So I was in a camp for 26 months and I went out, and I had to go to a psychiatric hospital for treatment there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the point, apparently, you want to make is clear to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I can have just one second to consult with my client, and then I will have more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we keep consultations within limits and otherwise to be done during breaks. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will endeavour, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this statement from 1994 goes into great detail, describing what you've already mentioned to us when your father was asked by Ramiz Alajbegovic to get villages to join the TO. The question I want to ask you is: Did you or your father ever help Mr. Alajbegovic to recruit other villages, apart from the Leleci village, to join the TO?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. And to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I interrupt you for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think to understand the answer, it is necessary to look at your question as it is recorded. I understood you to ask if you or -- and I quote: "... you or your father ever helped Mr. Alajbegovic to recruit other villages ... to join the TO?" The word "other" is missing and therefore the answer could be misunderstood. Please clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will. And I thank you, Your Honour, for the detail to attention that I missed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, there -- apparently I either misspoke, but to avoid confusion I'd like to ask you again: Did you or your father ever help Ramiz Alajbegovic to recruit over villages, other than Lelek, to join the Territorial Defence of the Republic of BiH?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, we never did that. That was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now you mentioned earlier, I believe, the 500 persons who were a part of the TO unit of the Republic of BiH in Radici. Am I correct that approximately half of this number were armed with automatic rifles, M48s, shorter military rifles; that is to say, military weapons rather than civilian hunting rifles?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were various weapons, hunting rifles, the M48 military rifles. I had such a rifle. That's why I'm familiar with it. There were also automatic weapons that the police had. That was in Novakovici, not in Radici. Because the lineup I was in was in Novakovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since Mr. Alajbegovic was the one that asked your father to ask the villagers of Lelek to join the TO, am I correct in assuming that Mr. Alajbegovic also had either a role in this TO or his own armed unit operating in the region? If you could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is possible that the police that went out was under his command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think we're at the one-hour point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are. Could you give us an indication as to how much time you would need after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe I used about approximately 10 minutes yesterday, one hour today, and I believe I should be able to finish within half an hour or 40 minutes in the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then you stay within the time-limits you indicated before. Could the witness already be escorted out of the courtroom. We'd like to see you back after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see Mr. Lukic has arrived in the courtroom. The Prosecution indicated that it would swap the two next witnesses. I think, as a matter of fact, that it would have been appropriate to suggest and seek permission to do that after we've heard from the Defence. Mr. Lukic, you are now here. The next witness the Prosecution would wish to call is Mr. Atlija. Any problems with this swap?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we are not going to finish his cross today, I can start, and probably they will have some time with Mr. Atlija. So we are ready to continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is appreciated. Your flexibility. And, Mr. Groome, you would agree with me that it would have been better not to indicate that you would, rather you are seeking permission to change the order at the very last moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wouldn't ordinarily do it, but a very unusual circumstances arose which I think the Chamber will learn about when the witness does testify. I think the Chamber will understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There may be good reasons why you want to swap. Nevertheless, the proper procedure is that you seek leave to do it and that's not the way in which it was announced.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, but again I would have been unable to produce the witness because of this very unusual circumstance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would then all could have been discussed at the moment you would have asked permission to do so. If it would have caused the Defence any problems, but apparently the flexibility of the Defence allows to proceed, as you suggested.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And just so the record is complete, Mr. Lukic and myself had three conversations last night about this witness and about the problem, so none of this is a surprise to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the Chamber was unaware --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just would like to correct my colleague. This was never mentioned to us, that there could be some kind of swap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's keep it as it is at this very moment. I wanted to emphasise that a swap at the last moment requires, first of all - and that apparently has been done - a conversation with the Defence, although the report on what the content of the conversation was is not clear, and then to address the Chamber and give all the information available at that time in order to receive permission to swap. We take a break, and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you may proceed once the witness is in the courtroom. Could he be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The transcript not yet states that we resumed. So we're still in recess, although apparently speaking. Madam Transcriber has corrected it, and the Chamber appreciates that she has done so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll continue, Mr. Hurko. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. For now I'd like to ask you some questions about this group whether it was one or two under Mr. Alajbegovic and Mr. Hadzibulic. First of all, sir, did you ever become aware, in 1992, of an organised attack that was carried out upon a military installation at Trovrh wherein --

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ever have occasion to become familiar with an event on the 4th of June, 1992 when there was an organised attack by armed Bosnian Muslims upon a military installation at Veliki Zep?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that both of these locations - that is to say, Trovrh and Veliki Zep - are part of Rogatica municipality?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about Trovrh. But Zepa is in Rogatica -- part of Zepa is in Rogatica municipality, whereas another part belongs to Han Pijesak. But as for Trovrh, I'm not sure whether it is in Rogatica or Gorazde. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In any event, those are all places near to the area --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge, sir, of an incident that occurred the 3rd through the 5th of June, 1992, wherein there was an attack on Boran village when Serb civilians were killed by armed Bosnian Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, you keep putting questions to me about places where I had never been. I was in the area between Rogatica, Gorazde, and Visegrad. That's where I was during the war, in that part of the country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now there are sometimes other ways of gaining knowledge. If you have no knowledge, just say, No, I have no knowledge. That sufficiently explains. Mr. Ivetic may not always be aware of what you know, what you observed, or what you heard from other persons. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, about the 14th of July, 1992, and the killings of Serbs in Drobnjaci and Duljevac. Did you hear about these?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of Drobnjaci and Duljevac. I've heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: To clarify, since the transcript indicates that you heard about "that," are you referring to knowing about the two villages of Drobnjaci and Duljevac, or are you referring to knowing about the killing of Serbs in those villages?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I know of the villages. I've heard of villages called Drobnjaci and Duljevac, but I don't know what happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, sir, that from May to August 1992 there was fighting going on between armed Bosnian Muslims and armed Serb forces throughout Rogatica municipality?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in the area where I was, there was only shelling of the villages at the time, and there was shooting from those villages towards -- from some villages towards Visegrad. As for the other side, I don't know about that. Whether there was any fighting or not, I didn't hear of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Allow me to move on, then, back to a point where you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, just for my understanding and perhaps for my colleagues as well. This is all about background, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Only background.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Only background.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps sometimes I would start with the foreground and then to the background. I mean, the statement of the witness is about detention, beatings during detention, persons being killed when they were detained, a witness being forced to beat his father. That is what is the core of his testimony. Now, the background, and you might even seek to agree with that, what we often see now is that witnesses are asked about whether they were aware that a Serb was killed, and that may even amount to a crime. I would not deny that. But it's all background, if I understand you well, and that there's no, at least from what we've heard now, on the most important elements of the testimony of this witness, there's no challenge to, if I could call it, the foreground, the matters I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think that also these matters are important to challenge the credibility of the witness and to see if there's any issue of partiality of the witness, and I believe that the areas I'm going into now will show that, in fact, we cannot rely upon this witness for everything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There were a few questions about the reliability of the witness. That's clear to the Chamber. But, again, background takes now approximately 80 per cent of the time in cross-examination rather than the core of what seems to be the testimony of the witness. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask about some -- the names of some Bosnian Muslim persons from the Rogatica area, and I'm going to ask you if you know them. Jamakovic, Lutvo?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Hasecic, Alem.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perkusic, Saudin.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unknown.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Two individuals: Bahulovic, Hapa and Bahulovic, Nane.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the names, but I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sabanic Samir.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Zagorica Muaz.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him. Just by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to those individuals that you indicated you either knew or had heard of, do you recall if they were members of either the Hadzibulic TO unit or Mr. Alajbegovic's MUP unit?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lutvo Jamakovic was a member of the MUP of Mr. Alajbegovic's. And the other one, probably Hadzibulic. Hadzibulic's men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would like to call up number 1D00212, which is a document -- and it's page, I believe, 4 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S. And I apologise, this is a partial translation so it's not a -- it's a draft translation, it's not a full translation. I will only deal with the parts that have been translated. And I apologise, it's page 3 in the B/C/S for this particular question. The item at the end the page, sir, in the B/C/S talks about various incidents, and it talks about these individuals whose names I have just read to you lighting up or I guess -- I guess razing the park hotel in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that it is a document. That doesn't come as a surprise to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you told us that there is only a partial translation and not a full translation, and yet you will deal only with a few pages. What is it? That's the relevant information the Chamber needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: This is an intelligence report. It was disclosed by the Prosecution. It was also used in the Karadzic proceedings. And I apologise, this is how it was disclosed to us. I'm not going to be seeking to introduce the document, I just want to ask the witness if he can verify information relating to these individuals who he has just named and whether he was knowledge of any of these incidents contained herein.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I take it individuals he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct. That's why I asked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or he has heard about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's why I asked before I presented the document, that he identified four individuals that he either knew or had heard about and what units they were parts of.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I could ask if we could see the first page of the document, just to see in e-court whether -- in the B/C/S, whether it contains any kind of a stamp or seal. And if it could be scrolled down to the bottom. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any information about this incident wherein these individuals that you named that were part of the both the same TO unit as yourself and Mr. Alajbegovic's MUP unit and the attack that they performed on the Park Hotel in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Park Hotel, I don't know anything about. Of all of this, I only know the Vodice village. There was a large nest there from which they fired on the Muslims. The Jamakovic that you mentioned, Lutvo Jamakovic, that's the person that I know. He gathered a group of men and they attacked that village and liberated it, and the machine-gun nest was no longer there. I don't know who was killed. This is all I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you know it by personal observation or did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard about it. I was nearby and I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From whom did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't recall anymore. But I heard it from several people, the civilians who were there. I can't remember exactly who it was I heard it from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have finished with this document since the witness has gone and given us the extent of his knowledge of Vodice.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to ask you: Are you familiar with an organised attack, or ambush I guess it was, that occurred at Jabucko Sedlo in Kopaci wherein an armoured Praga, artillery piece, was actually taken over by armed Bosnian Muslim forces in Rogatica municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I misspoke. When I said Rogatica, I meant Gorazde. But I believe, sir, that your answer did not come in -- did not enter the transcript. Could I ask you to please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But would now you also please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I would ask -- I would like to ask you if you are familiar with an organised attack or ambush, I guess it was, that occurred at Jabucko Sedlo wherein an armoured Praga, an artillery piece, and a tank were taken over by Bosnian Muslim forces? And I said Rogatica municipality but you corrected me that that is Gorazde municipality. Do you know of this event, sir?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to now turn to a topic that is related to some information that you gave when you testified in Sarajevo to the State Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the trial of Stojan Perkovic, 15th October 2009. First of all, sir, do you recall giving testimony in that case?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And maybe so that we can -- well, I apologise. The transcripts are only in English so I don't think they will be of assistance to the witness. But, sir, if you need to be refreshed about these items I'm going to ask you about, I will put up the transcript and I will read it to you. But I think it's a very simple issue. Do you remember in that case that you identified that you gave additional statements to the SIPA metro special police and also the Association of Women Victims of War? In B/C/S that would be "Zene Zrtava Rata."

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us when it was that you have given these statements and if you have copies in your possession?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have those copies and I can't really remember. It was five or six years ago that I made the statement to the Association of Women Victims of War. And as for SIPA, that was perhaps -- the statement that I made was perhaps half a year or a year before Perkovic was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, for the record the Defence was not provided those statements. We did ask the Office of the Prosecutor and they did indicate that they do not have them in their possession.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That's correct, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Were you approached by these organisations or did they approach you to make statements?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: They approached me to get that statement from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now I want to focus with you upon the statement given to the Women Victims of War Association. Am I correct that is headed by a Ms. Bakira Hasecic?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Are you or are have you ever been a member of that organisation headed by Ms. Bakira Hasecic?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, my information is that persons who have given statements to that organisation and are members receive a monthly stipend of up to 350 euros a month for their statement. Did you receive or have you ever received any stipend or money in exchange for giving your statement to the Women Victims of War Association?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it's not euros but marks. Yes, I did receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you for the correction, sir. Now I'd like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one -- Did you receive one stipend or did you receive it on a monthly basis; and, if so, for how long?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received them on a monthly basis and it has been going on for three years now. I've been a member of that organisation for three years, and this organisation includes people who were sexually abused. They may be members of the organisation. Those who are not victims of sexual abuse may not be members of this organisation. So once it was established what had happened to me at the camp, then I started receiving this stipend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, that means altogether over three years approximately 12.000, you say deutschemarks, but they do not exist anymore --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But I still receive that. That is the law. Everyone who was a victim of sexual abuse would receive that, and I still receive it to this day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it, therefore, your testimony that all victims get such a stipend on a monthly basis or only those who have given statements to the organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. There are quite a few people who have provided statements and they do not receive anything. It's only for those people who were sexually abused, who were raped and whatnot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can just clarify. Perhaps the Chamber will think it is me that's giving evidence, but the Bosnian money, despite -- for historical reasons is still referred to as deutschemarks even though Your Honour is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Actually, counsel is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's -- let's -- let's leave out this detail. We have an idea of the approximate amount of money involved and that's what the witness receives.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I was going to ask the witness to answer if that was ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think it needs clarification, Mr. Ivetic, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you say marks, are we talking about the convertible marks which have a fixed rate of exchange with the euro that are circulated in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina today, with the abbreviation KM.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That are in circulation today in Bosnia-Herzegovina, yes, and they have a fixed rate of exchange with the euro. And it's about -- it's the equivalent of around anywhere between 175 and 200 euros. Yeah, well, after what we've been through, you know, it's not bad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two marks to one euro, that's approximately. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, now I'd like to turn to your testimony about the direct interactions that you claim you had with General Mladic in 1994. First of all, sir, can you agree with me that you neither mentioned that in the two statements you gave to the BiH authorities 1994, nor these two statements that you've identified to SIPA and this association, nor the two statements that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was when I was exchanged. My first statement was given in 1994. I was taken to the court by this military unit in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and I think that's where I gave the statement. Now, the later statement that I provided in November when I went to the Security Services Centre, I began giving my statement but then a shell struck that building and we had to flee to the basement. So then I started giving it again, but then we had to flee to the basement three times. Now you can imagine what was like for me after I had spent 26 months in the camp. We were only able to put together some six pages or so at this time, and I just couldn't think of what it was that I could tell them. As for the other statement about Perkovic, to do with the Perkovic thing, they wanted me to talk about the people who had been arrested, and that's why I didn't provide the statement. The same is true for the Karadzic case. I didn't provide any statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you testified in two proceedings in the State Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina wherein you also never mentioned this encounter with General Mladic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, not for those two cases, because it wasn't necessary. Because it had to do with other crimes committed by those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's focus on the encounter itself. Can you describe for us how General Mladic was dressed?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a military camouflage uniform, as far as I can recall. I think he didn't have any cap on his head. There was a lot -- there were a lot of troops around him. They all wore camouflage uniforms. That's what the Serbs wore. He had some insignia, but I didn't really know much about them. He was a general or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just to be clear, when Mr. Mladic asked if those of you working were loyal or captured, am I correct that Mr. Mladic was told that you were, in fact, loyal citizens rather than captured prisoners? And I'm referring to what Mr. Bojic told him.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bojic, or, rather, Mladic asked Mr. Bojic who are these men? And Bojic said, These are prisoners from the Rogatica camp. And then Mladic asked, Are they loyal or were they captured? And Bojic said, They are loyal. And then he said, Well, let them come out from the ditch where we were hiding. When we got out --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me focus on the aspect of your -- of this testimony. Isn't that correct, sir, that there were other people there also performing tasks from, for instance, Satorovici, this area where they had tents set up that -- where these people were sleeping with -- were co-habitating with the Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the village of Satorovici?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, among other things.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Satorovici village, also Tmorni Do. These were loyal villages until 1993. In November 1993 they were all taken to Rogatica camp and then we were assigned to provide food to those people. This was as of April 1st, 1994, and onwards, and this is when we had this meeting with Mladic. There were people from Satorovici from the camp. I can't recall all the names. I know, for instance, Vatar [phoen] Semso, Mujo Jasarevic, Trusmo Mufti and so on. They were there when Mladic was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How far away were you from General Mladic during this encounter with him?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we got out it was more than 4 or 5 metres, when we stood there as he was saying that to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you or any of the other prisoner there correct Bojic or advise General Mladic of the fact that you were prisoners or captured combatants rather than loyal citizens?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't say anything. It was only Bojic who spoke.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, there is a great risk of confusion. Captured was earlier referred to as captured at the front line as a combatant. Now, if you're not captured at the front line as a combatant, apparently you're considered to be loyal, but loyal, in such a context, does not mean - and I'll ask the witness what it may not mean. When you had an encounter with Mr. Mladic, were you at that time free to go wherever you wanted to go, or were you not free to move as you wished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that moment, we didn't dare go anywhere where we wanted to go ourselves. We just went to where they took us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ivetic, where there seemed to be a kind of a loyal and being captured at the front line, there may be a category of persons being loyal, and, at the same time, captured but then in a different way. So we should avoid any confusion about that, and there may be not be the dichotomy which is suggested in the -- in the conversation that we heard about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, my question was then did -- so Bojic misrepresented the situation to General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think, as a matter of fact, it's the wording used. We have heard from the witness whether he was free to go at that moment, and certainly it was -- if we under -- if we take that as a starting point, it certainly, the conversation, did not give the details and gave a dichotomy which may not be one which existed in reality. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, at that time, sir, neither you nor any of the other individuals there brought to the attention of General Mladic the conditions under which you were being treated in detention. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were trembling, we were shaking. None of us dared speak, none of us prisoners who were working there. He only talked to Vinko. He was the warden of the prison in Rogatica, and he talked to hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, in fact, sir, do you know the -- the location where this took place? Could you describe that for us? Isn't this, in fact, rather far away from the detention facility where you were being detained?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say maybe 15, 20 kilometres away from the prison that we were. But when we were brought in on the 1st of April, that's when the operation against Gorazde took place, and we took food, ammunition, everything else towards Trovrh. The hill of Trovrh. When we had a break for about two or three days, a group did not go out to take food there. Then the military truck came one morning and said that 10 or 15 of us should go on this truck somewhere else, and we went elsewhere. We went to this other place, not the place where we had taken food before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You've already given us all this information during the direct examination. My focus was on the place where you had the encounter with Mr. Mladic. Am I correct that that is not located near the detention facility?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the witness not answered that question, 15 to 20 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise. I missed that part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I also observe that you are about at the time you indicated you would need. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have approximately six minutes or seven minutes of questions remaining, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to move to another topic of your testimony. At paragraphs 51 through 60 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could Mr. Mladic lower his voice. Most likely to be achieved by taking off his earphones when he consults with members of the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, just one last question about that -- about the encounter with Mr. Mladic before --

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you for a second. Very often Mr. Mladic is showing me something with his finger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic, if that is the case, and we may verify that, would you refrain from making any gestures, either approving or disapproving. I saw, for example, before the break that when you apparently happy in the way in which Mr. Ivetic conducted his cross-examination, it was thumbs up. You should refrain from that. I said that yesterday to you. I repeat it today. And if it continues, then please be aware that the Chamber may take measures which might be similar to the ones we took last week. Please be aware of that. This is a clear warning to you. We'll review, during the break, or later today, whether you made such gestures. And you may remain seated when I address you. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As I was sayings, sir, one final question about the encounter with Mr. Mladic before I move onto my last topic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mladic can consult with Mr. Lukic during the break. So it should stop now at this very moment. Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic, consultation in the break which will be in 20 minutes from now. Please proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this encounter with Mr. Mladic: Am I correct it is near the Jabucko Sedlo or Tritak [phoen] location?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the name of this place is. It belongs to Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move to another topic of your testimony at paragraphs 51 through 60 of your statement, which is P164. While we wait for that to come up, sir, can I ask you: Before the conflict, did you take much interest in politics?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Am I correct that during the conflict - that is to say, before you were captured - you did not have occasion to follow the politics going on in Rogatica during that time?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And during your detention in the various locations you have testified to, during that time-period, I suspect you also did not have occasion to follow politics in Rogatica. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In which period?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: From August 15th, 1992, until the time that you were exchanged, you did not have occasion to follow politics in Rogatica during that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, as far as the Crisis Staff in Rogatica is concerned, you never were present for any of their meetings, were you?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Therefore, I'm confused, sir, how it is that you are able to give quite detailed information about the composition of the Crisis Staff of Rogatica at these paragraphs of your statement. Am I correct, sir, that most of this information in paragraphs 51 through 60 of your statement actually was given to you by others, including either security organs in Sarajevo or Ms. Bakira Hasecic's organisation or others helping you to prepare for your testimony before the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no one did that. I heard about that while I was in prison from Serbs. These people that you are referring to and that you have in mind, Rajko Kusic, everybody else. Tell me their names and I will tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Tell us how precisely how you know Jadranko Vukovic was called Captain on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a teacher in Rogatica before the war. And some dogs were brought to Rogatica and he trained these dogs, and he was a captain at the Crisis Staff. That's what they called him. He was supposed to train these dogs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the question was how do you know that on the Crisis Staff they used to call him captain? How do you know that is what they called him in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These commanders in prison, they mentioned that. And that's what they said, that they were on the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How is it that you know Radomir Furtula commanded the attacks on Rogatica, Ustiprace, and Gorazde as is stated in paragraph 56 of your statement? I'm told that there is a problem with the translation. Could you tell us how it is that you know Radomir Furtula commanded the attacks on Rogatica, Ustiprace, and Gorazde as is stated in paragraph 56 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: SEFIK HURKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radomir Furtula was born in Rogatica and he was a military man before the war. He held the rank of major. He came several times --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I stop you here. Please carefully listen to the question. In your statement you say: "I know he commanded the attacks on Rogatica, Ustiprace, and Gorazde." How do you know this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I knew him before the war. He was born in 1957. He was a military man. He was a major. And he came to Rogatica --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
